 Amentum Reports Fourth Quarter and Fiscal Year 2026 Results 
 Annual Revenues of $13.8 billion 
 Annual Net Income of $338 million; Annual Adjusted EBITDA of $1,132 million 
 Annual Diluted Earnings Per Share of $1.38; Annual Adjusted Diluted Earnings Per Share of $2.51 
 Annual Operating Cash Flow of $627 million; Annual Free Cash Flow of $583 million 
 Backlog of $48.3 billion; Book-to-Bill - 1.0x Fourth Quarter, 1.1x Full Year 
 Reduced Net Debt to $3.1 billion and Net Leverage to 2.7x 
 Board Authorizes First-Ever $500 million Share Repurchase Program 
 CHANTILLY, VA., November 23, 2026 — Amentum Holdings, Inc. (“Amentum” or the “Company”) (NYSE: AMTM), a leading advanced engineering and technology company, today announced results for the year ended October 2, 2026 and issued guidance for fiscal year 2027. 
 “Amentum closed fiscal year 2026 with strong execution, delivering 50 basis points of margin expansion, increasing earnings per share and free cash flow by 13%, securing $17 billion in contract awards, and completing all major integration milestones,” said Amentum Chief Executive Officer John Heller. “As we enter fiscal year 2027, we remain focused on accelerating organic growth, driving operational excellence across the enterprise, and aligning the business with long-term demand trends. Combined with a disciplined capital allocation strategy, including our newly authorized $500 million share repurchase program, these priorities support our continued focus on creating long-term shareholder value.” | Summary Operating Results | Three Months Ended | Year Ended |

 GAAP Results 
 Fourth quarter revenues decreased 8% year-over-year driven by a 9% impact from an extra week in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025, partially offset by the ramp-up of new contract awards. For the year, revenues decreased by 4% driven by a 5% impact that includes an extra week in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025, the transition of certain contracts from consolidated to unconsolidated joint ventures, and fiscal year 2025 divestitures as well as impacts from the government shutdown; partially offset by the ramp-up of new contract awards and growth on existing programs. Fourth quarter and full year operating income increased as a result of strong

 Adjusted EBITDA increased 1% for the fourth quarter and 3% for the full year driven by continued progress on our margin expansion initiatives including a favorable mix shift and strong operational performance. Adjusted Net Income and Adjusted Diluted Earnings Per Share increased primarily as a result of the strong operational performance and lower interest expense.

See Unaudited Non-GAAP Financial Measures at the end of this press release for more information and a reconciliation of our selected reported results to these non-GAAP measures. 
 Digital Solutions revenues decreased 2% in the fourth quarter driven by a 10% impact from an extra week in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025, partially offset by the ramp-up of new contract awards in critical digital infrastructure and space systems and technologies. For the year, revenues increased 3% driven by the ramp-up of new contract awards and growth on existing programs; partially offset by a 4% impact that includes an extra week in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025 and the fiscal year 2025 divestiture of Rapid Solutions. Adjusted EBITDA increased 1% for the fourth quarter and full year as a result of strong program performance and the increased revenue volume, respectively. 
 Global Engineering Solutions revenues decreased 12% in the fourth quarter driven by a 8% impact from an extra week in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025 as well as the expected ramp-down of historical programs. For the year, revenues decreased by 9% driven by a 5% impact that includes an extra week in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025, the transition of certain contracts from consolidated to unconsolidated joint ventures, and a fiscal year 2025 divestiture as well as the expected ramp-down of other historical programs. Adjusted EBITDA increased 2% in the fourth quarter and 4% in the full year as a result of continued progress on our margin expansion initiatives, favorable contract mix, and strong program performance. 
 Cash Flow Summary 
 In the fourth quarter, Amentum generated $392 million of net cash from operating activities and used $24 million and $303 million in investing and financing activities, respectively. Net cash provided by operating activities was driven by strong cash earnings, disciplined working capital management, and reflects one less pay cycle compared to the prior year quarter. Net cash used in investing activities included $22 million in capital expenditures. Net cash used in financing activities consisted primarily of $287 million in voluntary principal payment on the Term Loan B. As of October 2, 2026, Amentum had $521 million in cash and cash equivalents and $3,574 million of gross debt. With net leverage reduced to 2.7x, Amentum has strengthened its financial position, providing greater flexibility for disciplined and opportunistic deployment. 
 Share Repurchase Authorization 
 Subsequent to quarter end, the Company’s Board of Directors authorized the repurchase of up to $500 million of the Company’s common stock. The share repurchase program provides additional flexibility to deploy capital as part of the Company’s disciplined capital allocation strategy. 
 2 
 Backlog and Contract Awards 
 As of October 2, 2026, the Company had total backlog of $48.3 billion, which includes an approximately $1.5 billion de-booking related to contract changes at NASA, compared with $47.1 billion as of October 3, 2025, an increase of 2.4% driven by $15.0 billion in net bookings and 1.1x book-to-bill. Funded backlog as of October 2, 2026 was $6.0 billion, compared with $5.6 billion as of October 3, 2025, an increase of 8.0%. 
 Notable Highlights 
 • NGA Integrated Campus Support (NICS) – The National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (NGA) awarded Amentum an $800 million ten-year contract to deliver technology-enabled solutions that maximize the performance of critical facilities and systems at NGA Washington. The award builds on Amentum’s successful track record of supporting critical infrastructure for national security missions at NGA and across the U.S. government and its allies across the globe. 
 • Navy Integrated Training Environment (NITE) 2 – The U.S. Navy awarded Amentum a new $700 million five-year contract to provide comprehensive operations and engineering solutions for the Navy’s live, virtual, and constructive integrated environment. Under this contract, Amentum will use secure AI and data analytics to enhance maintenance and operations, improve system readiness, and modernize systems for complex training scenarios. 
 • Australia Nuclear Submarine Shipyard Program – The Australian Naval Infrastructure (ANI) selected an Amentum-led joint venture as its Capability Partner to support the delivery of a nuclear-powered submarine construction yard in South Australia, providing program and construction management. This ten-year program reinforces Amentum’s position as a trusted industry partner, leveraging its extensive global nuclear experience in waterfront infrastructure, waste management, and regulatory in support of supporting global nuclear capabilities. 
 • U.S. Army Germany Site Operations – The U.S. Army awarded Amentum a new $375 million single-award indefinite delivery, indefinite quantity contract with a six-year ordering period to strengthen U.S. Army mission readiness across 21 installations in Germany. Through this award, Amentum will leverage its global expertise and advanced digital solutions to enhance operational efficiency, modernize installation support, and enable mission-critical operations. 
 • U.K. Nuclear Infrastructure & Remediation Solutions – The United Kingdom nuclear site operator Sellafield Ltd selected an Amentum-led joint venture as a preferred supplier for the nuclear Projects and Asset Care Execution (PACE) program valued up to $2.8 billion over an initial duration of nine years and an optional six-year extension. Amentum will support spent fuel management and retrievals mission through its full lifecycle capabilities, including engineering and design, installation, plant modification, project management and ongoing asset care. Formal award of the framework agreement will follow when final contractual arrangements are concluded. 
 • Navy Counter-Unmanned Systems (C-UxS) – The U.S. Navy awarded Amentum a $145 million single-award indefinite delivery, indefinite quantity contract with a five-year ordering period to support the U.S. Navy’s modernization of advanced counter-unmanned systems through research, development, testing, and integration of next-generation technologies to enhance operational capabilities. 
 • Classified Intelligence Awards – Amentum was awarded over $350 million in intelligence contracts, including an award supporting enterprise IT and operational objectives to deliver systems engineering, network and infrastructure support, cybersecurity, and platform integration.

These items are uncertain, depend on various factors and could have a material impact on GAAP reported results for the relevant period. 
 3 
 Webcast Information 
 Amentum will host a conference call beginning at 8:30 a.m. Eastern time on Tuesday, November 24, 2026 to discuss the results for the fourth quarter and fiscal year ended October 2, 2026. The conference call will be webcast simultaneously to the public through a link on the Investor Relations section of the Amentum website at amentum.com . After the call concludes, a replay of the webcast can be accessed on the Investor Relations website. 
 About Amentum 
 Amentum is a global leader in advanced engineering and technology solutions, trusted by the United States and its allies to address the most complex challenges in science, security and sustainability. Our people apply boundless imagination to challenge convention. Safety, collaboration and well-being are integral to our success. Headquartered in Chantilly, Virginia, we have over 45,000 employees in more than 70 countries across all 7 continents. 
 Visit us at amentum.com to learn how we advance the future together.

 Important factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from such plans, estimates or expectations include, among others: changes in U.S. or global economic, financial, business and political conditions, including changes to governmental budgetary priorities and tariffs and the ongoing conflicts in Europe and the Middle East; our ability to comply with the various procurement and other laws and regulations; risks associated with contracts with governmental entities; reviews and audits by the U.S. government and others; changes to our professional reputation and relationship with government agencies; the occurrence of an accident or safety incident; the ability of the Company to control costs, meet performance requirements or contractual schedules, compete effectively or implement its business strategy; the ability of the Company to retain and hire key personnel, and retain and engage key customers and suppliers; the failure to realize the anticipated benefits of the 2024 transaction with Jacobs Solutions Inc.; potential liabilities associated with shareholder litigation or other settlements or investigations; evolving legal, regulatory and tax regimes; and other factors set forth under Item 1A, Risk Factors in the annual report on Form 10-K (the “Annual Report”), and from time to time in documents that we file with the SEC. Any forward-looking statement speaks only as of the date on which it is made, and we assume no obligation to update or revise such statement, whether as a result of new information, future events or otherwise, except as required by applicable law. 
 Non-GAAP Measures 
 This release includes the presentation and discussion of Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA Margin, Adjusted Net Income, Adjusted Diluted Earnings Per Share, Free Cash Flow, and Net Leverage, which are not measures of financial performance under Generally Accepted Accounting Principles in the United States (“GAAP”). These non-GAAP measures should be considered only as supplements to, and should not be considered in isolation or used as substitutes for, financial information prepared in accordance with GAAP. Management of the Company believes these non-GAAP measures, when read in conjunction with the Company’s financial statements prepared in accordance with GAAP and, where applicable, the reconciliations herein to the most directly comparable GAAP measures, provide useful information to management, investors and other users of the Company’s financial information in evaluating operating results and understanding operating trends by adjusting for the effects of items we do not consider to be indicative of the Company’s ongoing performance, the inclusion of which can obscure underlying trends. Additionally, management of the Company uses such measures in its evaluation of business performance, particularly when comparing performance to past periods, and believes these measures are useful for investors because they facilitate a comparison of financial results from period to period. The computation of non- 
 4 
 GAAP measures may not be comparable to similarly titled measures reported by other companies, thus limiting their use for comparability. 
 Definitions of applicable non-GAAP measures and reconciliations to the most directly comparable GAAP measures are provided elsewhere in this release. 
 In addition to the above non-GAAP financial measures, the Company has included backlog, net bookings, and book-to-bill in this release. Backlog is an operational measure representing the estimated amount of future revenues to be recognized under negotiated contracts, and net bookings represent the change in backlog between reporting periods plus reported revenues for the period. Book-to-bill represents net bookings divided by reported revenues for the same period.  • Navy Integrated Training Environment (NITE) 2 – The U.S. Navy awarded Amentum a new $700 million five-year contract to provide comprehensive operations and engineering solutions for the Navy’s live, virtual, and constructive integrated environment. Under this contract, Amentum will use secure AI and data analytics to enhance maintenance and operations, improve system readiness, and modernize systems for complex training scenarios. 
 • Australia Nuclear Submarine Shipyard Program – The Australian Naval Infrastructure (ANI) selected an Amentum-led joint venture as its Capability Partner to support the delivery of a nuclear-powered submarine construction yard in South Australia, providing program and construction management. This ten-year program reinforces Amentum’s position as a trusted industry partner, leveraging its extensive global nuclear experience in waterfront infrastructure, waste management, and regulatory in support of supporting global nuclear capabilities. 
 • U.S. Army Germany Site Operations – The U.S. Army awarded Amentum a new $375 million single-award indefinite delivery, indefinite quantity contract with a six-year ordering period to strengthen U.S. Army mission readiness across 21 installations in Germany. Through this award, Amentum will leverage its global expertise and advanced digital solutions to enhance operational efficiency, modernize installation support, and enable mission-critical operations. 
 • U.K. Nuclear Infrastructure & Remediation Solutions – The United Kingdom nuclear site operator Sellafield Ltd selected an Amentum-led joint venture as a preferred supplier for the nuclear Projects and Asset Care Execution (PACE) program valued up to $2.8 billion over an initial duration of nine years and an optional six-year extension. Amentum will support spent fuel management and retrievals mission through its full lifecycle capabilities, including engineering and design, installation, plant modification, project management and ongoing asset care. Formal award of the framework agreement will follow when final contractual arrangements are concluded. 
 • Navy Counter-Unmanned Systems (C-UxS) – The U.S. Navy awarded Amentum a $145 million single-award indefinite delivery, indefinite quantity contract with a five-year ordering period to support the U.S. Navy’s modernization of advanced counter-unmanned systems through research, development, testing, and integration of next-generation technologies to enhance operational capabilities. 
 • Classified Intelligence Awards – Amentum was awarded over $350 million in intelligence contracts, including an award supporting enterprise IT and operational objectives to deliver systems engineering, network and infrastructure support, cybersecurity, and platform integration.
